lens: A heavy signing day carried into the new week: MarineMax agreed a ~$1.5B Blackstone take-private (Wells Fargo, Evercore), Ryman bought the Grande Lakes Orlando resort for $1.38B (BofA, JPMorgan), Archer took three Boeing aerospace units (JPMorgan, Moelis), and Bio-Techne and Theravance filed merger proxies — a broad covered-bank slate even as advisory stocks sold off.

stories.headline: MarineMax to be acquired by Blackstone’s Safe Harbor for ~$1.5B; Wells Fargo advises MarineMax, Evercore advises Safe Harbor
stories.why_it_matters: MarineMax (NYSE: HZO) entered a definitive agreement to be acquired by Safe Harbor Marinas (a Blackstone Infrastructure portfolio company) for $53.00/share in cash, a ~$1.5B enterprise value. The release names Wells Fargo as exclusive financial adviser to MarineMax (sell-side) and Evercore as exclusive financial adviser to Safe Harbor (buy-side). A sponsor take-private of a public retailer/marina operator runs financing, antitrust and shareholder-vote workstreams to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Wells Fargo (MarineMax) and Evercore (Safe Harbor) — a ~$1.5B sponsor take-private runs committed-financing, antitrust and proxy diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: MarineMax agrees to $53.00/share sale to Safe Harbor (~$1.5B)

stories.headline: Ryman Hospitality to acquire the Grande Lakes Orlando resort for $1.38B; BofA and JPMorgan advise Ryman
stories.why_it_matters: Ryman Hospitality Properties (NYSE: RHP) agreed to acquire the Grande Lakes Orlando resort (JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton brands) from Trinity Investments for $1.38B, a 12.5x trailing Adjusted EBITDAre multiple, expected to close Q3 2026. The release names BofA Securities and J.P. Morgan as financial advisers to Ryman (buy-side). A large single-asset hotel acquisition runs real-estate, financing and franchise-diligence workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage BofA and JPMorgan (Ryman) — a $1.38B trophy-resort acquisition runs property, financing and franchise diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: Ryman agrees to acquire Grande Lakes Orlando ($1.38B)
Expected close

stories.headline: Archer to acquire Boeing’s Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid; JPMorgan advises Boeing, Moelis advises Archer
stories.why_it_matters: Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR) agreed to acquire three Boeing units — autonomous-flight developer Wisk Aero, drone maker Insitu, and airspace-software firm SkyGrid — with Boeing (NYSE: BA) taking an equity stake in Archer (terms undisclosed; Insitu ~$200M annual revenue). The release names J.P. Morgan as financial adviser to Boeing (sell-side) and Moelis & Company as financial adviser to Archer (buy-side). A carve-out of multiple aerospace/defense units into a public acquirer runs separation, regulatory (defense/ITAR) and equity-consideration workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage JPMorgan (Boeing) and Moelis (Archer) — a multi-unit aerospace/defense carve-out runs separation, ITAR/regulatory and equity-consideration diligence a secure room organizes.

deal_clock.event: Archer agrees to acquire Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid from Boeing

stories.headline: Bio-Techne files its merger proxy for the ~$73/share Merck KGaA acquisition; Goldman advises Bio-Techne, Guggenheim and JPMorgan advise Merck
stories.why_it_matters: Bio-Techne (Nasdaq: TECH) filed a preliminary merger proxy (PREM14A) for its acquisition by Merck KGaA (Darmstadt, Germany) at $73.00/share, advancing the ~$11.3B life-sciences deal to a shareholder vote. The filing names Goldman Sachs as Bio-Techne’s financial adviser (fairness opinion, sell-side) and Guggenheim Securities and J.P. Morgan as financial advisers to Merck KGaA (buy-side). A large-cap cross-border life-sciences merger runs antitrust (multi-jurisdiction), disclosure and shareholder-vote workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Goldman (Bio-Techne) and Guggenheim/JPMorgan (Merck KGaA) — a ~$11.3B cross-border life-sciences merger runs multi-jurisdiction antitrust and proxy diligence a secure room organizes to close.

deal_clock.event: Merck KGaA agrees to acquire Bio-Techne ($73.00/share)
Preliminary merger proxy (PREM14A) filed

stories.headline: Theravance Biopharma files its merger proxy for the Zymeworks acquisition; Lazard advises Theravance

stories.headline: Two Piper Sandler mortgage/bank tie-ups filed: MITT–Cherry Hill mortgage-REIT merger and HBT–Tri-County
stories.why_it_matters: Piper Sandler surfaced on two filed FIG combinations Aug 10. It is exclusive financial adviser to AG Mortgage Investment Trust (MITT) on its stock-and-cash merger with Cherry Hill Mortgage (CHMI) — a $117.5M implied value, 29% premium (BTIG advised CHMI). Separately, Piper Sandler is financial adviser to HBT Financial on its acquisition of Tri-County Financial Group — HBT’s twelfth merger since 2007. Bank/mortgage-REIT consolidation runs regulatory-approval and shareholder-vote workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Piper Sandler (MITT and HBT) — consolidation among mortgage REITs and community banks runs regulatory-approval and proxy diligence a secure room keeps organized across parallel deals.

deal_clock.event: MITT–Cherry Hill and HBT–Tri-County combinations announced

stories.headline: Advisory stocks slide to open the week even as the M&A calendar stays hot — EVR -2.6%, LAZ -3.5%, JEF -2.3%
stories.why_it_matters: Equities were modestly lower into the Aug 10 close (S&P -0.06%, Nasdaq -0.32%, Dow -0.11%), with the VIX near ~15.5 and the 10Y around ~4.69%. The notable move was in the advisory complex itself: Evercore (-2.6%), Lazard (-3.5%) and Jefferies (-2.3%) all sold off, an odd divergence on a day that produced a heavy slate of covered-bank signings (Ryman, MarineMax, Boeing/Archer). The disconnect between advisory-stock weakness and robust deal flow is a reminder that pipeline strength shows up in mandates before it shows up in the tape.
stories.suggested_action: Lean on the deal flow, not the stock tape — a soft session for advisory shares alongside a busy signing day is a cue to keep the conversation on live-process execution and room readiness.

market_snapshot.macro_note: A soft start to the week for stocks and a sharper pullback in advisory names: the S&P 500 slipped -0.06% (~7,753), Nasdaq -0.32% (~26,605) and Dow -0.11% (~53,976) into the Aug 10 close, with the VIX near ~15.5 and the 10Y around ~4.69%. The advisory complex sold off hardest — EVR -2.6%, LAZ -3.5%, JEF -2.3% (JPM bucked it, +0.6%) — an odd divergence given a genuinely heavy M&A signing day (Ryman, MarineMax, Boeing/Archer all with covered banks). Index and bank-stock values are Aug 10 closes; VIX and the 10Y are live Aug 11 morning levels.

talking_point.quote: The tape didn’t reward advisory names Monday — Evercore, Lazard and Jefferies all sold off — but the mandate flow told the opposite story: a ~$1.5B MarineMax take-private, Ryman’s $1.38B resort buy, Archer’s carve-out of three Boeing units, and fresh Bio-Techne and Theravance proxies, all with banks we cover. Pipeline strength shows up in signings before it shows up in the stock. Which of your live processes has the nearest diligence milestone this week?
talking_point.use_with: Consumer/real-estate, industrials/aerospace, and healthcare coverage teams (esp. Wells Fargo, Evercore, BofA, JPMorgan, Moelis, Goldman, Lazard)
talking_point.context: Pairs an advisory-stock pullback with a genuinely busy signing day — a way to redirect the conversation from the tape to live-process execution.
